title: D-Dimer: Pretest Probability and False Positives
subject: Pathology Markers
preview: D-dimer is sensitive to fibrin turnover but nonspecific; infection, pregnancy, surgery and age can increase it.
quickRevision: D-dimer is sensitive to fibrin turnover but nonspecific; infection, pregnancy, surgery and age can increase it.
High clinical probability for pulmonary embolism generally requires appropriate imaging or another definitive approach, not D-dimer reassurance.
Different laboratories and assays use different units and cutoffs, so interpret the report accordingly.

sections.title: Interpret the result in context
points: D-dimer is sensitive to fibrin turnover but nonspecific; infection, pregnancy, surgery and age can increase it.
Its diagnostic value depends on pretest probability and use of a validated rule-out strategy.

sections.title: Clinical interpretation & next steps
points: High clinical probability for pulmonary embolism generally requires appropriate imaging or another definitive approach, not D-dimer reassurance.
Different laboratories and assays use different units and cutoffs, so interpret the report accordingly.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A positive D-dimer cannot confirm pulmonary embolism by itself.

quiz.question: When is a negative D-dimer most useful in suspected PE?
options: Appropriate low-risk or selected intermediate-risk rule-out pathways
Every postoperative patient regardless of risk
Patients with high clinical probability without imaging
